name: Samson of Dol
knownFor: A British monk and bishop, trained at Eltut's school, who crossed by way of Cornwall to Brittany and founded the monastery of Dol, known from a Life of uncertain date and a signature at a council of Paris.
dates: Signed a council at Paris that Friedrich Maassen dates between 556 and 573. Thomas Taylor reckons from the Life that he was made bishop probably in 521, and born about 486 if he was then thirty-five; both years are Taylor's inference
place: Of Demetia (Dyfed) in Wales, by the Life; his father of Dyfed and his mother of Gwent, by Taylor's summary; Eltut's school at Llantwit; Ireland; Cornwall; Dol in Brittany, where he died
role: Monk, abbot and bishop; founder of the monastery of Dol

traces: The Life says he founded Dol and many other monasteries throughout almost the whole province, and that he went to King Hiltbert, whom Taylor names as Childebert, to free a captive named Judual.
Taylor reports pilgrimages from Britain and Brittany to his tomb at Dol, a church and parish bearing his name near Fowey, and a church at Southill dedicated to him.
remembered: Taylor: later Lives of saints tried to rival this one's miracles, and it "actually furnished the mould into which many of them were cast".
A later Life of Illtud, printed by W. J. Rees, counts him among Illtud's pupils with Paulinus, Gildas and Dewi.

uncertain: Nearly all that is known of him comes from one Life, a book of miracles whose writer gives no name. The writer says he drew on an old man of Samson's family and on writings of the deacon Henoc.

When the Life was written. Taylor accepts 610 to 615, following Abbé Duine, who found in it nothing borrowed from writings later than the end of the 500s. Taylor reports that Fawtier called the work spurious and did not accept its writer's statements on its authorship and origin; Duine and Professor Loth answered him.

The council signature is a second witness to the man, not to the Life's details. It reads only "Samson", with no see; Maassen's note gives Dol with a question mark, and his index lists him as bishop of Dol.
His birth and consecration years are Taylor's reckoning from the Life's notes on the day of his consecration, and the Life gives no year.
